Introduction {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} ## The Personal Assistant :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-right} ![](images/basics/gemini-assistant.png){width=100%} ::: ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-left}
NotebookLM as (Junior) Assistant **Clear Instructions** → Better Results ::: :::: ## How to "Talk" to NotebookLM?
```{mermaid} %%{init: { 'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'primaryColor': '#ffffff', 'primaryTextColor': '#374151', 'primaryBorderColor': '#e5e7eb', 'lineColor': '#9CA3AF', 'secondaryColor': '#f9fafb', 'tertiaryColor': '#ffffff', 'fontFamily': 'system-ui', 'fontSize': '24px', 'nodeSpacing': 150, 'rankSpacing': 150 } }}%% flowchart LR subgraph Input[" "] direction TB A["Prompt"] D["Sources"] style A fill:#FFED00,color:#374151,stroke:#FFED00,padding:30px style D fill:#FFED00,color:#374151,stroke:#FFED00,padding:30px end subgraph Model[" "] direction TB B["NotebookLM"] style B fill:#ffffff,color:#374151,stroke:#e5e7eb,padding:30px end subgraph Output[" "] direction TB C["Output"] style C fill:#FFED00,color:#374151,stroke:#FFED00,padding:30px end A --> B D --> B B --> C style Input fill:#ffffff,stroke:#e5e7eb,color:#374151,stroke-width:1px,padding:50px style Model fill:#ffffff,stroke:#e5e7eb,color:#374151,stroke-width:1px,padding:50px style Output fill:#ffffff,stroke:#e5e7eb,color:#374151,stroke-width:1px,padding:50px linkStyle default stroke:#9CA3AF,stroke-width:2px ```
::: {.tiny-text .fragment .fade-up} | **Element** | **Description** | |----------------|---------------------------------------------------------| | **Sources** | The documents that have been added to the notebook | | **Prompt** | The question or instruction | | **NotebookLM** | Uses Google's Gemini to understand and respond | | **Output** | Text, mind map, or audio response | ::: ## Limitations of NotebookLM :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/basics/error.png){width="100%"} **Factual Errors**: Can produce incorrect information ::: ::: {.column width="33%" .fragment .fade-up } ![](images/basics/hallucination.png){width="100%"} **Hallucinations**: Produces fabricated content (less common than other AI tools) ::: :::: ## Prompting Basics :::: {.columns} ::: {.column} In this presentation, prompts are displayed as follows: ```md This is an example prompt ```
The prompt can be copied using the icon in the top right.
::: :::: # The First Notebook {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} A notebook is a collection of sources for a specific project. ## Notes on Slide Structure Most slides follow the structure shown here. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/screenshot.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left }
Here you'll find the instructions. The steps shown serve as guidance. ::: :::: . . . :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="56%" } ::: {.callout-note .fragment .fade-up} This section provides additional context or tips. ::: ::: :::: ## Opening NotebookLM :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/notebooklm-open.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left .custom-small}
On your own device: [🔗 Open NotebookLM](https://notebooklm.google/) ::: :::: . . . :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="56%" } :::{.callout-note .fragment .fade-up} NotebookLM cannot delete or edit original files in Google Drive. ::: ::: :::: ## Creating a New Notebook :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-00.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
To create a new notebook, select: **+ Create new** ::: :::: ## Adding Sources :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-000.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left .custom-small}
Select your own document (ideally PDF or Google Slides) :::{.small-text} The [EU AI Act](images/notebooklm/EU-AI-ACT.pdf) (PDF) is used as an example here ::: Add the document. ::: :::: . . . :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="56%" } ::: {.callout-note .fragment .fade-up} Up to 300 sources can be added: **(1)** PDF, PPT, Excel, Audio, Images **(2)** Google Docs or Google Slides **(3)** Website or YouTube **(4)** Copied text **(5)** Web search ::: ::: :::: ## Three Main Areas :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="80%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-0000.png){width="80%"} ::: ::: {.column width="20%" } ::: :::: . . . :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="20%" .tiny-text } **Sources area**: Upload and manage documents. ::: ::: {.column width="30%" .tiny-text } **Chat area**: Ask questions and get answers based on your own documents. ::: ::: {.column width="30%" .tiny-text } **Studio area**: Generate and save outputs like summaries, study guides, and notes. ::: :::: ## Automatically Generated Summary :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" } ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-01.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"}
::: :::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="56%" } ::: {.callout-note .fragment .fade-up} The summary is automatically generated. ::: ::: :::: ## Save as Note :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-08.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
**1** In the **Chat area**: Select **Save to note**. ::: :::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="56%" } ::: {.callout-note .fragment .fade-up} **2** The note appears in the "Notebook" within the **Studio area**. ::: ::: :::: ## Opening the Note :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-09.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
Click on the note in the **Studio area** to open it in a new window. ::: :::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="56%" } ::: {.callout-note .fragment .fade-up} Saved response notes are not editable. ::: ::: :::: # Chat {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} Ask the model questions about source material or give instructions for actions. ## Selecting Sources :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-1.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
Use the checkbox for each source to include or exclude specific sources that the model should use to answer the question. ::: :::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="56%" } ::: {.callout-note .fragment .fade-up} Sources can be added or removed by selecting **+ Add** or deselecting individual sources in the **Sources area**. ::: ::: :::: ## Asking the Model Questions :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-11.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
Enter a question in the chat window. ::: {.tiny-text .fragment .fade-up} For example: ```md What are the key insights from this document? ``` ::: ::: :::: ## Citations :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-011.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
Selecting a citation leads to the corresponding location in the document. ::: :::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="56%" } :::{.callout-note .fragment .fade-up} Hovering over a citation displays the complete cited text. ::: ::: :::: ## Clear Chat :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-012.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
To delete the chat history, select **Refresh**. ::: :::: ## Customize Chat :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-02.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
Navigate to **Configure notebook** in the chat area. ::: :::: Conversation style and response length can be customized. ## Conversation Style: Default :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-04.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
::: :::: **Default**: Ideal for general research and brainstorming tasks. ## Conversation Style: Analyst :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-05.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: :::: **Analyst**: Ideal for business-oriented strategy and decision-making. ## Conversation Style: Guide :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-06.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: :::: **Guide**: Use the notebook as a knowledge base or help center. ## Conversation Style: Custom :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-07.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left} ::: :::: **Custom**: Optimal for defining a specific role. **Response Length**: Response length is also selectable: *Default*, *Longer*, and *Shorter*. # Mind Map {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} Mind maps visually summarize uploaded sources and display main topics as well as related ideas as a branched diagram. ## Creating a Mind Map :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-12.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"}
**1** In the **Chat area**, select the mind map chip. **2** The mind map appears in the **Studio area**. ::: :::: ## Interacting with a Mind Map :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-13.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"}
Open the mind map in the **Studio area**. Expand or collapse branches with **>**. Change view, download, or close (top right corner). ::: :::: ## Select Nodes to Ask Questions :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-16.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"}
Select a node to ask questions and chat about this specific topic. ::: :::: # Audio Overview {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} Audio overviews are audio discussions between AI moderators that provide summaries of topics in the uploaded sources. ## Choose Output Language :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-audio-settings.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"}
**1** Navigate to **Settings**. **2** Select the **Output language**. ::: :::: Audio overviews can be created in over 50 languages. ## Creating an Audio Overview :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-audio-1.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"}
**1** In the **Studio area**, navigate to the "Audio overview" section. **2** Under "Deep dive conversation," select **Generate**. ::: :::: ## Interacting with an Audio Overview :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-audio-interactive.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"}
Select **Interactive mode** (BETA). Select **Play audio**. While listening, select **Join** and ask a question. ::: :::: ## Managing the Audio Overview :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-audio-options.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"}
Change speed, download audio, or delete. Select "More" to: :::{.small-text} **1** Change the playback speed. **2** Download the audio as mp3. **3** Delete the audio overview. ::: ::: :::: ## Custom Audio Overviews :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-audio-custom.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} *If an audio overview already exists, it must be deleted first.* **1** In the **Studio area**, navigate to the "Audio overview" section. **2** Under "Deep dive conversation," select **Customize**. :::{.tiny-text} Enter a custom prompt (max. 500 characters). Example prompt (adjust placeholders): ```md Create an audio overview for [TARGET_AUDIENCE] with a [TONE] tone. Focus on [FOCUS] and aim for [DURATION]. Cover key insights with concrete examples. PLACEHOLDERS [TARGET_AUDIENCE] = Kärcher management [TONE] = professional [FOCUS] = practical insights [DURATION] = 8-10 min. ``` ::: ::: :::: # Study Guide {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} Automates the process of identifying key vocabulary and formulating relevant quiz questions. ## Quiz Questions and Glossary :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-23.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
**Studio area**: Click on **Study Guide**. ::: :::: Creates a quiz for self-assessment and a glossary with key terms. ## Opening the Study Guide Note :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-24.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
**Studio area**: Open the newly created note. Take a look at the questions, answer key, and glossary. ::: :::: # Briefing Document {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} Summarizes key topics, definitions, and timelines from the provided sources. ## Creating an Overview of Key Topics :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-25.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-up}
**Studio area**: Click on **Briefing doc**. ::: :::: ## Opening the Briefing Document :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-26.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-up}
**Studio area**: Open the newly created note. Take a look at the briefing document. ::: :::: # FAQ {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} Creates "question-answer" pairs to get a general, structured overview of the main topics in the documents. ## Creating FAQs :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-27.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-up}
**Studio area**: Click on **FAQ**. ::: :::: Creates a "question-answer" pair format. ## Opening FAQ :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-28.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-up}
**Studio area**: Open the newly created note. Take a look at the FAQ. ::: :::: # Timeline {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} Quickly understand the sequence of events in the documents. Perfect for creating historical overviews, tracking project progress, or outlining a biography. ## Creating a Timeline :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-29.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
**Studio area**: Click on **Timeline**. ::: :::: Timeline and person directory based on the provided sources. ## Opening the Timeline :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-30.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
**Studio area**: Open the newly created note. Take a look at the timeline. ::: :::: # Discover Sources {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} Enables discovering relevant sources from the web and importing them directly into the notebook. ## Discovering New Sources :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-34.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
**Sources area**: Click on **Discover**. Enter any topic of interest (EU AI Act was entered here). ::: :::: ## Selecting and Adding Discovered Sources :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-35.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
Select the discovered sources you want to keep. ::: :::: ## Using New Sources :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-36.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left}
Select the sources to work with and create new content (like mind maps, etc.). ::: :::: # Notes {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} Organize information and add your own thoughts. ## Creating & Adding Notes :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-21.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-up}
**Studio area**: In the **Notes** section select **Add note**. Text can be written or pasted into this note. ::: :::: Up to 1,000 notes can be created per notebook. ## Converting Notes to Sources :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-22.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-up}
**Studio area**: Open the note. Select **Convert to source**. :::{.small-text .fragment .fade-up} *To convert all notes to sources:* Click **More** in the **Notes** section in the **Studio area**. Select **Convert all notes to sources**. ::: ::: :::: . . . Your own notes can be added to the sources. # 2. Exercises - Quick Wins {background-gradient="linear-gradient(to bottom, #FFDE00, #FFDE00)"} **Goal:** Become familiar with NotebookLM. ## Meeting Preparation :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-00.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left }
1. Open [NotebookLM](https://notebooklm.google.com) 2. Select **Create new** 3. Upload a presentation (optional: add related documents) 4. Ask the following question in chat: :::{.tiny-text .fragment .fade-up} ```markdown Create a summary of the key insights I need to know. Make it conversational, as if a colleague were briefing me over coffee. ``` ::: 5. Save result as note 6. Create an audio summary and check the result 7. Create a mind map and check the result ::: :::: . . . :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="56%" } :::{.callout-note .fragment .fade-up appearance="simple"} **Having difficulties?** Simply raise your hand or ask in chat. Problems will be solved together! ::: ::: :::: ## Meeting Preparation 2 :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-012.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left }
1. Use the same notebook 2. Click **Refresh** in the **Chat area** 3. Ask the following question in chat (replace the placeholder "Finance" with your own area): :::{.tiny-text .fragment .fade-up} ```markdown Extract the 5 most important decisions or recommendations from this document. Explain for each the rationale and potential impacts on [AREA]. [AREA] = "Finance" ``` ::: 4. Save the result as **Note** 5. Review the result ::: :::: ## Invitation to Share Experiences :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/use-cases/share-2.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left }
**A discussion in chat about:** - The most important insights or "aha moments". ::: :::: ## Email Action Items :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-audio-custom.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left } 1. Open [NotebookLM](https://notebooklm.google.com) 2. Select **Create new** 3. Copy your email thread (print as PDF) and add to sources 4. Use the following prompt in chat: ::: {.fragment .tiny-text .fade-up} ```md Summarize this email thread as 1. Decisions made 2. Action items (who/what/when) 3. Open questions 4. Next required steps ``` ::: 5. Save the response as **Note** for future reference 6. Review the results: Is the summary helpful? ::: :::: ## Customized Audio Summary :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-audio-custom.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left } 1. Open [NotebookLM](https://notebooklm.google.com) 2. Select **Create new** 3. Upload a (complex) document of your choice 4. Navigate to the "Audio overview" section in the Studio area 5. Under "Deep dive conversation" select **Customize** 6. Enter this customized prompt (max. 500 characters): ::: {.fragment .tiny-text .fade-up} ```md Create an audio overview that covers - Key insights to be drawn from this document - Important decisions or required actions - Critical information for the next meeting - Main points that can be shared with colleagues Make it conversational, as if a colleague were briefing over coffee. Focus on what's actionable and immediately useful. ``` ::: 7. Select **Length** (use *Default*), create the audio overview and listen to the first two minutes. ::: :::: ## Extracting Insights from Videos :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-audio-custom.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left } 1. Start a new notebook (click the black icon in the top left) 2. Click **+ Create new** to start a new notebook. 3. To add the video, click **YouTube** and enter a link. For example: :::{.tiny-text .fragment .fade-up} ```txt https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3gWb3LNfX28 ``` ::: 3. Use the **Mind map** function to get an overview of the video's structure and main messages. 4. Use prompts to extract useful information, e.g.: ::: {.fragment .tiny-text .fade-up} ```md Provide step-by-step instructions for using the Kärcher window vacuum for streak-free window cleaning, from assembly to maintenance. ``` ::: ::: :::: # 3. Use Cases {background-color="#FFED00"} **Goal:** Master use cases that are actually applied. ## Select Use Case ::: { .fragment } - A. **Presentation Preparation**: *Convert reports into presentation outlines* - B. **Competitive Analysis**: *Analyze multiple competitor documents simultaneously* - C. **Training Accelerator**: *Transform manuals into engaging content* - D. **Communication Clarity**: *Precise communication* - E. **Domain-Specific Use Case**: *Use a domain-specific use case* ::: ## A: Presentation Preparation **Challenge:** Board presentation due Friday :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-00.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left } 1. Open [NotebookLM](https://notebooklm.google.com) 2. Select **Create new** 3. Upload the report or data documents 4. Use the following prompt in chat (adjust target audience and length): ::: {.tiny-text .fragment .fade-up} Example prompt (adjust target audience and length): ```markdown Create a presentation outline with - 5 compelling talking points - Supporting data for each point - 3 key insights for executives - 10 potential Q&A scenarios Target audience: "Board of Directors" Presentation length: "30 minutes" ``` ::: 5. Save the result as **Note** 6. Create an **Audio summary** to practice the presentation 7. Create a **Mind map** for a visual overview ::: :::: ## B: Competitive Analysis **Challenge:** Understanding the competitive landscape :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-00.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left } 1. Open [NotebookLM](https://notebooklm.google.com) 2. Select **Create new** 3. Upload multiple competitor materials 4. Use the following prompt in chat: :::{.tiny-text .fragment .fade-up} Example prompt: ```markdown Compare these competitor documents and identify: - Their main advantages - Gaps in their offerings - Opportunities for Kärcher - Price/positioning differences Create a strategic summary. ``` ::: 5. Save the result as **Note** 6. Ask follow-up questions about specific competitors 7. Create a **Mind map** to visualize the competitive landscape ::: :::: ## C: Training Accelerator **Challenge:** Making technical content engaging :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment .fade-up} ![](images/notebooklm/nlm-00.png) ::: ::: {.column width="40%" .fragment .fade-left } 1. Open [NotebookLM](https://notebooklm.google.com) 2. Select **Create new** 3. Upload the technical training materials 4. Use the following prompt in chat (adjust placeholders): :::{.tiny-text .fragment .fade-up} Example prompt (adjust placeholders): ```markdown Transform this technical manual into - 10 practical use cases/examples - Interactive Q&A for self-assessment - Checklist with key points - Common mistakes to avoid Make it engaging for [TARGET_AUDIENCE]. [TARGET_AUDIENCE] = "Kärcher Project Managers" ``` ::: 5. Save the result as **Note** 6. <script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
